title: Existence of a normalized derived coefficient presentation
statement: Let C and D be sites essentially small in the coefficient universe, and let inverse be a left exact left adjoint to direct on set sheaves. Fix a coefficient ring A, the constant ring sheaves, algebraic inverse-image lifts IA and IR, ring sheaves RX, RI, RY, compatible algebra maps aX, aY, aI and structural map c as in [def-pur-ringed-coefficient-counit-presentations]. Let o be an OrdinaryPresentation with IA.modules additive, and assume the four derived categories exist. Then there is a DerivedPresentation o, with exact coefficient restrictions, canonical derived adjunctions and the specified tau and kappa representative equations. This statement does not assert the counit square or any coefficient-change result.

proof.text: Restriction of scalars preserves the underlying abelian sheaf. Kernels are computed sectionwise and cokernels by sheafifying sectionwise cokernels; hence both restrictions are exact. Let x and y be their exact derived functors with the canonical termwise factorization isomorphisms. Inverse image of constant-A modules is exact: its underlying set sheaf is the geometric inverse image, so it preserves kernels and epimorphisms; additivity gives exactness. This supplies CoefficientExactness and the invertible constant-coefficient comparison.

Take the universal left derived functor of o.pull, computed by flat-term K-flat resolutions, and the universal right derived functor of o.pushR, computed by K-injectives. Apply the derived adjunction theorem to o.adjR. Its representative Hom characterization gives exactly r.homFormula, for every complex P and K-injective I. Do the same for o.adjA. The resolving-class computation gives flatComparison, and exactness of IA.modules makes a.epsilon an isomorphism on every complex.

Whisker the left-derived counit r.epsilon with exact coefficient restriction x. It remains the absolute left-derived counit, since it is invertible on the flat-term K-flat resolving class. Compose the termwise factorization of y and the counit a.epsilon with the degreewise ordinary scalarUnit. The universal left-derived lift of this composite is tau. Evaluating its factorization equation at P gives tauFormula. This constructs a natural transformation on the whole derived category; the universal property, rather than a choice of a representative map for each object, ensures independence of resolutions.

Compare the two factorizations of the composite ringed-topos direct image through constant coefficients. Exact coefficient restriction identifies its own right derived functor with the termwise localization. The normalized right-derived composition isomorphisms therefore give kappa: r.right followed by y is isomorphic to x followed by a.right. If I is K-injective and j:restriction(aX)(I) to T is a K-injective resolution, the composition formula says its component is the class of ordinaryKappa followed by pushA(j), followed by a.eta and the inverse resolution identifications. These are precisely the factors of kappaFormula. Assemble all these data into DerivedPresentation. No counit square or coefficient-change naturality is asserted here.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_derivedPresentation
    (aX : constantRing JX A ⟶ RX) (aY : constantRing JY A ⟶ RY)
    (aI : constantRing JX A ⟶ RI)
    (haI : (sheafCompose JX (forget CommRingCat.{r})).map aI =
      IA.ringUnderlying.inv ≫ inverse.map
        ((sheafCompose JY (forget CommRingCat.{r})).map aY) ≫ IR.ringUnderlying.hom)
    (hc : aI ≫ c = aX)
    (o : OrdinaryPresentation direct geom IA IR c aX aY aI)
    [IA.modules.Additive]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (modules RX)] [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (modules RY)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (modules (constantRing JX A))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (modules (constantRing JY A))] :
    Nonempty (DerivedPresentation o)
